html: The Nespelem are an Interior Salish people of north-central Washington State, from the Nespelem River where it meets the Columbia. They speak the same dialect as the Sanpoil, part of the Colville-Okanagan language, and lived on Columbia salmon and gathered roots and berries. They avoided war with the United States and signed no treaty. In 1872 their land became part of the Colville Reservation, home of the Colville and other confederated tribes, and the town of Nespelem became its agency town. Chief Joseph of the Nez Perce, exiled there with his band in 1885, is buried at Nespelem.
